description: List the channel kinds an agent can have and what each needs before it works: a schedule, a webhook secret, or a browser authorization. The built-in kinds come first (cron, heartbeat, webhook, mcp, slack, telegram), then the catalog entries Valet curates for services that send events, such as GitHub. A catalog entry a built-in kind already covers is not repeated, and console, chat, and email, which create_channel does not make, are left out. Each says whether a call here can finish the setup or a person has to finish it in a browser. Each row gives the kind's name, whether it is built in, a description, what it needs, and the slots to fill. Requires connecting a Valet account.

org_name.description: The Valet organization a channel would be created in. The catalog is the same for every organization; this names the one the answer points the next step at. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

name: list_catalog_channels

channels.description: The channel kinds an agent can have, built-in kinds first, then catalog entries.

builtin.description: True for a built-in kind, false for a catalog entry.

description.description: What the channel does. Absent when the entry has none.

kind.description: The channel_kind that create_channel takes to make this channel: the built-in kind itself, or the kind of the catalog entry, which is webhook for a service that sends events.

name.description: The built-in kind, or the catalog entry's name.

needs.description: What the channel needs before it works: schedule when the call names when it fires, secret when it needs a signing secret, which a person enters through set_env_vars secret_names, browser when a person finishes it in a browser, none when it works once created.

slots.description: Names of the secret slots a catalog entry asks for. Absent when it names none.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

title: List catalog channel kinds
